docs.title: chronon
docs.text:
chronon is an independent learning project: a staging slice of a time-shared quantum-datacenter platform. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or connected to IQCC or Quantum Machines, and it never contacts their services. The "device" is a simulation.

Status: rung 1. The local site runs (kind, Cilium, Argo CD and the platform components), and the API serves /healthz over TLS with HTTP/2. The task and state services don't exist yet.

  • Architecture: what lives where.
  • Client contract: the API the unmodified client expects, with source references.
  • Build log: decisions, failures and measured numbers.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text: Status: the local site (rung 1) exists: kind, Cilium, Argo CD, cert-manager, the CNPG operator, Valkey, Argo Workflows, and a Gateway serving /healthz. Each component below gets its own page under Components once it's built; until then it's listed as planned.

docs.text: Path Holds Status src/chronon/auth.py RS256 provider-token verification: signature, window, roles, projects planned src/chronon/contract.py Pydantic models mirroring the client (datasets, task status) planned src/chronon/api/app.py task API: /task/{backend}/{workflow}, /task/{backend}/{id}, DELETE, /metrics /healthz only src/chronon/state/app.py state service: /{backend}/state/, /{backend}/state/{id}, /children, /{backend}/timeseries/ planned src/chronon/queue.py Valkey queue, fifo and per-user fair modes planned src/chronon/db.py SQLAlchemy models for tasks and datasets; Alembic planned src/chronon/worker/ sim-qpu device loop and its synthetic physics planned src/chronon/arc/ Stark-map chunk and merge CLIs planned src/chronon/instrument/ mock VISA-like instrument planned tests/unit/ unit tests exists (client patch) tests/contract/ the real client against a running site planned vendor/iqcc-cloud-client-0.20.0/ the client sdist, read-only reference exists scripts/client_patch.py points the real client at chronon, blocks upstream exists scripts/bootstrap/local.sh the substrate: kind, Gateway API CRDs, Cilium, images, Argo CD, root app exists scripts/ (others) connect helper, rehearsal, token minting planned docker/Dockerfile images: base (exists) and arc (planned) targets partly clusters/local/ the local site: kind bootstrap, Argo CD apps, values, overlays exists platform/ shared components: cilium, cert-manager, pki, cnpg, valkey, argo-workflows, gateway exists backends/sim-qpu/, backends/arc/ per-backend manifests planned services/k8s/base/ API and state Deployments, Services, HTTPRoutes API only docs/ this site (MkDocs Material) exists .github/workflows/ci.yml gates, images, docs deploy exists

docs.title: Build log
docs.text: Timestamps are IDT (UTC+3). Newest entries at the bottom.

docs.title: Mon 19 Oct 2026: scaffold
docs.text:
16:35 · Tooling on an Intel Mac. brew install uv kind kubeconform kustomize sat for over 10 minutes building libgit2 and xz from source. Root cause: Homebrew no longer ships prebuilt bottles for these formulae on Intel macOS 15, so every dependency compiles locally. Fix: stopped brew and installed the official release binaries into ~/.local/bin after checking each SHA-256 against the project's published checksums (uv 0.13.1, kind v0.33.0, kubeconform v0.8.0, kustomize v5.8.3). Prevention: on this machine, prefer upstream release binaries over brew for single-binary tools.

16:45 · Vendored the client. iqcc_cloud_client-0.20.0.tar.gz from PyPI, SHA-256 a7c038b8…ef791a matches PyPI's published digest. Extracted unmodified into vendor/iqcc-cloud-client-0.20.0/, with its BSD-3 LICENSE.

16:50 · The client's state URL can't be overridden by argument. IQCC_Cloud.state is a property with a default parameter (computers.py:747). Properties take no arguments, so the default is always used, and the constructor calls it three times. Decision: replace the property on the class before construction (scripts/client_patch.py), plus a second layer that guards httpx.Client.send against the upstream domain. Unit tests use httpx.MockTransport, so even a broken guard can't reach the network.

16:55 · Two holes in the planned check gate, found before first use. 1. The manifest loop ended in … | kubeconform … || true. The || true swallowed kubeconform's failure, so the gate could never fail. And without pipefail, a failing kustomize build piped empty input into kubeconform, which passes. Fix: SHELL := /bin/bash, .SHELLFLAGS := -eu -o pipefail -c, and an if instead of && … || true. 2. The upstream-domain grep used git grep, which only searches tracked files. Before the first commit nothing is tracked, so it passed while checking nothing. Fix: git grep --untracked. On its first run it flagged CLAUDE.md, which names the domain in the rule forbidding it; CLAUDE.md is now on the allow-list.

17:00 · pyright vs an upstream annotation. The client annotates url as AnyUrl but defaults it to a str and concatenates it as one (computers.py:44, 379). We pass a str through cast(Any, …) with a comment, rather than silencing the rule.

Numbers - uv lock: 136 packages resolved in 5.3 s (time uv lock). - uv sync --extra dev: 2 min 29 s wall, 379 s CPU. Some dependency built from source on Intel macOS (time uv sync --extra dev). - make check: 10 unit tests pass in 1.8 s.

20:02 · Correction found during the explain-back. The first draft of the client-patch page said that importing the patch "too late" would be caught by the send guard. It wouldn't: the guard is installed by the same import, so a process that never imports the patch, or constructs the client first, is unprotected. The page now says so. The defences are structural (entry points import the patch themselves) plus an OS-level hosts sinkhole. A second finding from the same discussion: any calibrator could push a qmm_capabilities dataset, which the client unpickles. The state service will refuse writes of reserved types (docs/contract.md).

docs.title: Mon 19 Oct 2026: rung 1, the local site
docs.text:
20:15 · argocd CLI skew. Homebrew's argocd was 2.14.5, and the server is v3.5.5. Installed the v3.5.5 binary (checksum verified) and ran brew unlink argocd (reversible with brew link argocd), because /usr/local/bin comes before ~/.local/bin on PATH.

20:18 · Two upstream facts checked before writing manifests. helm show values cilium/cilium --version 1.20.3: enableAlpn: false by default, and gatewayClass.create: auto creates the GatewayClass only if the Gateway API CRDs already exist, so the CRDs go first. Argo CD v3.5.5 docs (operator-manual/health.md): Application health was removed in 1.8 and must be restored for app-of-apps sync waves. The bootstrap patches argocd-cm.

20:28 · CI rejected the workflow file. Root cause: hashFiles() isn't allowed in a job-level if: (only status functions are), so GitHub failed the whole file before any job ran. Fix: drop the condition; the Dockerfile exists.

20:29 · Committed an editor swap file (src/chronon/api/.app.py.swp, from vim). Untracked it, kept it on disk, and now ignore *.swp. Prevention: look at git status before git add -A.

20:30 · kind load failed for valkey/valkey:8.1.10: ctr: content digest sha256:d2a1…: not found. Root cause: Docker Desktop uses the containerd image store (docker info: io.containerd.snapshotter.v1), which keeps a multi-platform image's index but only the amd64 layers. kind exports the index, and ctr import --all-platforms on the node looks for the missing platforms. Images we build (chronon:dev) are single-platform and load fine. Fix: the nodes pull the one Docker Hub image themselves (one image, one replica, far under the anonymous rate limit). Rejected: retagging a locally rebuilt single-platform copy under the upstream tag.

20:36 · valkey and chronon OutOfSync right after "successfully synced". Root cause: fields the API server defaults (StatefulSet claim-template fields, the HTTPRoute's default PathPrefix / match) aren't in git. Argo's diff for SSA apps (structured-merge) reports them as drift. Fix: Server-Side Diff (controller.diff.server.side: "true", stable since v3.1), plus a controller restart.

20:45 · Sync-wave deadlock. chronon (wave 1) stayed Progressing, so the gateway app (wave 2) was never created. Root cause: an HTTPRoute is Progressing until a Gateway accepts it, and its Gateway was in a later wave. Fix: Gateway to wave 0 (it only needs the wave −1 certificate); routes stay with their services. The in-flight root sync was pinned to the old revision, so it needed argocd app terminate-op root. Side lesson: since Argo CD 3.0, per-resource health isn't stored in .status.resources; use argocd app get.

20:51 · Rung 1 DoD passes. curl --http2 -v --cacert .certs/ca.pem https://api.chronon.test:8443/healthz → ALPN: server accepted h2, SSL certificate verify ok, HTTP/2 200. The client's transport (httpx.Client(http2=True, http1=False)) also gets HTTP/2 200. argocd app list: 8/8 Synced/Healthy. cilium status: OK. Hubble UI: HTTP 200 over a port-forward.

Numbers - kind create (3 nodes, v1.37.0): 91 s; Cilium to status OK: 200 s (bootstrap stage stamps, .logs/bootstrap-1.log). - Argo CD install and rollout: 109 s; full bootstrap re-run on an existing cluster: 156 s (.logs/bootstrap-2.log). - docker build --target base: 1 min 19 s cold (time docker build …).

docs.title: Built with Claude Code
docs.text:
chronon is built in pair with Claude Code: Claude Code writes most of the code, and Orel makes every design decision and reviews every change.

The working rules are in CLAUDE.md at the repository root. The short version:

  • Decisions first. Architectural choices are made explicitly and recorded as ADRs with the options that were rejected and where they break.
  • Gates before "done". make check (format, lint, strict types, unit tests, manifest validation, and a grep that keeps the upstream domain out of the code) must pass, and contract tests must pass against a running site for anything touching the API.
  • Explain-back. After each component, Orel explains it back, and the explanation lives under Components.
  • Honest docs. Pages describe only what exists; shortcuts are named.

Failures and their root causes are recorded in the build log.

docs.title: The client contract
docs.text: This page is the source of truth for the task and state API as iqcc-cloud-client 0.20.0 uses it. Every behaviour cites the vendored source: vendor/iqcc-cloud-client-0.20.0/src/iqcc_cloud_client/<file>:<line>. Paths below are relative to that directory. chronon implements the server side of this contract; it never changes the client.

docs.title: How chronon points the client at itself
docs.text:
Upstream defaults: the task API is https://cloud.i-qcc.com (computers.py:44), the state service https://state.i-qcc.com (computers.py:747-761) and the datastore https://ds.i-qcc.com (computers.py:100).

IQCC_Cloud.state is a property with a state_service_url default argument. A property can't receive arguments, so the default is always used, and the constructor calls it three times (computers.py:108, 114, 137). The URL can't be overridden per call. scripts/client_patch.py therefore replaces the property on the class before any instance is constructed, and also:

  • requires an explicit api_token, because without one the constructor reads ~/.config/iqcc_cloud/config.toml, whose url key overrides the argument (computers.py:61-73);
  • disables .data (the datastore, computers.py:763-779);
  • guards httpx.Client.send so a request to the upstream domain raises before it leaves the process.

docs.title: Transport
docs.text: Behaviour Source Task client: http2=True, http1=False for every URL except http://localhost:8000. Over TLS, that means ALPN must negotiate h2; an HTTP/1.1-only server fails the handshake. computers.py:371-376, 443-448, 474-479 State client: http2=True, http1=False always. There's no localhost exception. state.py:29-31 Headers on every request: Authorization: Bearer <token>, User-agent: iqcc-cloud-client/0.20.0. computers.py:91-96 Timeouts: 60 s default; task polls use 10 s, then 5 s. computers.py:107, 424-441, 464-471

docs.title: Errors (both services)
docs.text:
• Success means exactly HTTP 200 (httpx.codes.OK). A 201 or 202 is treated as an error (computers.py:343, state.py:65, 126, 146, 194, 332). POST endpoints must therefore return 200.
  • The task client prints the status phrase, then tries r.json()["detail"]. If the body isn't JSON it raises ConnectionError; otherwise ValueError (computers.py:343-354).
  • The state client calls r.json()["detail"] on errors without a try (state.py:94-95, 129-130, 155-156, 214-215, 361-362). A non-JSON error body (for example a plain-text 500 from a proxy or a framework default) raises inside the client, and inside the constructor that kills IQCC_Cloud(...) (computers.py:108).
  • Rule for chronon: every error from either service is {"detail": "<human-readable, actionable>"}, including 500s.

docs.title: Constructor side effects
docs.text:
IQCC_Cloud(backend, api_token, url) immediately makes these state calls:

Call Expected by the client chronon serves Source get_latest("summary") a summary dataset, or none a seeded summary dataset computers.py:108-110 get_latest("key_qua") an ML-KEM public key record, or none; errors are caught none (an empty list), so end-to-end encryption is off computers.py:113-133 get_latest("qmm_capabilities") base64 of a pickle, which the client unpickles; errors are not caught none (an empty list), ever computers.py:136-141

get_latest(t) is list(datatype=t, limit=1) followed by get(id). An empty list returns None (state.py:217-233).

Observation: because the client unpickles qmm_capabilities, whoever can write that dataset can run arbitrary code on every client that connects. key_qua is similar: whoever writes it chooses the key clients encrypt to. push is open to any calibrator, for any type. Rule for chronon: the state service refuses writes of the reserved types qmm_capabilities and key_qua, whatever the caller's role.

docs.title: summary dataset (data shape)
docs.text:
Read by summary() (computers.py:650-745), run() (computers.py:294-310) and _available_on_demand() (computers.py:630-648):

{
  "online": true,
  "description": "…",
  "state": {"<datatype>": {"description": "…"}},
  "ondemand": {"<workflow>": {"description": "…", "schema": {"…": "JSON Schema"}}},
  "runtime": {"visa": {}}
}
  • online, description, state, ondemand and runtime.visa are all indexed without .get, so a missing key is a KeyError (computers.py:664-668, 673, 639, 729).
  • If "state" is a key of state, summary() calls get_latest("state").timestamp (computers.py:679-685). With no state dataset that is None.timestamp, an AttributeError. List state only once a state dataset exists.
  • transpiler_target in state triggers a native-gates table (computers.py:689-727). Optional.

docs.title: State service API
docs.text:
Client method Request Response (200) Source list GET /{backend}/state/?skip&limit[&datatype][&producer] [DatasetMeta], newest first state.py:33-95 get GET /{backend}/state/{id} Dataset; the client warns if backend differs state.py:133-156 push POST /{backend}/state/ body {type, data, comment, parent_id} Dataset; restricted to role calibrator (docstring) state.py:97-131 trend GET /{backend}/timeseries/?jsonpath&skip&limit[&datatype][&producer] [{id, t, value}], newest first state.py:158-215 list_children GET /{backend}/state/{id}/children?skip&limit[&type][&producer] [DatasetMeta] state.py:298-362

Notes:

  • The filter is called datatype on list and trend, but type on list_children (state.py:58 vs state.py:325).
  • Trailing slashes matter: /state/ and /timeseries/ end in /; /state/{id} and /children don't.
  • trend(..., terminal_output=True) plots only values whose type(...) is exactly int or float (state.py:199). A one-element list isn't plotted, so the server unwraps a single match to a scalar.
  • Models (interfaces.py:5-55): DatasetMeta = id, timestamp, type (≤60), comment (≤300), producer (≤60), parent_id (nullable). Dataset adds backend (≤60) and data (any JSON). timestamp is parsed by pendulum, so an ISO 8601 string is used.

docs.title: Task API
docs.text:
Step Request Response Source Submit POST /task/{backend}/{workflow} with the JSON payload 200 {"task_id": "…"} computers.py:379-397 Poll GET /task/{backend}/{task_id}, about once per second 200 {"task_status": …, "task_result": "<JSON string>"} computers.py:423-485 Revoke DELETE /task/{backend}/{task_id} on Ctrl-C ignored computers.py:399-408
  • run() validates the payload against summary.ondemand[workflow].schema client-side before sending (computers.py:308-318). Server-side validation only guards non-client callers.
  • Polling loops while task_status == "PENDING" (computers.py:430), then while it is RECEIVED or STARTED (computers.py:461). Any other value ends the wait. SUCCESS is reported as success; anything else is printed in red (computers.py:513-534).
  • task_result is passed to json.loads with a complex-number decoder (computers.py:496, utilities.py:155-158). It must always be a valid JSON string encoding an object, because .get("encrypted") is called on the result (computers.py:499). Use "{}" while not finished.
  • A finished result is {"result": {…}, "stdout": "…", "stderr": "…"}. A non-empty stderr is printed as an error, and the strings Execution timed out after or Timeout occured while waiting for result streams make the client raise TimeoutError (computers.py:515-527, 626-627).
  • Complex numbers are encoded as {"__type__": "complex", "data": [re, im]} (utilities.py:155-158).
  • execute() (QUA programs) posts to /task/{backend}/qua (computers.py:259-267). chronon doesn't implement it.

docs.title: Special result keys
docs.text:
With terminal_output=True the client pops these keys from result and pretty-prints them (computers.py:545-623):

Key Shape Source __total_python_runtime_seconds number (printed %.3f) computers.py:599-605 __qpu_execution_time_seconds number (printed %.3f) computers.py:606-612 __fridge_info {"<name>": {"temperature_kelvin": float, "unix_timestamp": epoch}} computers.py:613-620 __pre_hook, __sync_hook, __post_hook {"stdout": str, "stderr": str} computers.py:567-598

In chronon these values come from the simulated device and are labelled as simulated.

docs.title: Tokens
docs.text: Behaviour Source The provider key pair is RSA 2048. The private key is PEM PKCS#8; the printed public key is PEM PKCS#1. cli.py:86-98 Tokens are RS256 JWTs with payload {"user_id", "qpu": {"<backend>": {"from", "to", "access": [roles], "project": [projects]}}, "expires"}, where expires == to, all in Unix seconds. tokens.py:54-67 There are no standard exp, iat, kid or jti claims. A verifier checks expires and the window by hand, and can't key revocation on a token ID. tokens.py:54-65 The client reads its own roles by decoding without verifying the signature (display only; the server must verify). computers.py:143-159 The role that may push datasets is calibrator. tokens.py:48, state.py:104-105

docs.title: ADR-0002: One Argo CD per site; Cilium and Argo CD are bootstrap-managed
docs.text: Status: accepted (draft) · Mon 19 Oct 2026

docs.title: Context
docs.text: The platform is meant to run at more than one site from the same repo. The CNI and the GitOps engine are special: pods can't get addresses before the CNI exists, and Argo CD is itself pods.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Where it breaks A. One Argo CD per site, same repo, clusters/<site>/ app-of-apps. CNI and Argo CD installed by a script. Cilium and Argo CD upgrades are a scripted step, not a commit; drift in those two isn't auto-healed. B. Hub-and-spoke: one central Argo CD managing every site The WAN link to the hub becomes a dependency for every site's changes; one compromised hub reaches every site. C. ApplicationSet with a cluster generator Good for many similar clusters; adds a templating layer that hides what a single site runs. Worth it at 5+ sites, not 1–2. D. Argo CD also manages Cilium after bootstrap (adoption) A bad Cilium commit auto-syncs, breaks pod networking, including Argo CD's, and Argo can no longer roll it back.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: A. scripts/bootstrap/local.sh runs kind → Gateway API CRDs → Cilium → images → Argo CD → the root Application. Everything else is an Application, ordered by sync waves (−2 cert-manager; −1 CNPG operator, PKI; 0 Valkey, Argo Workflows, Gateway; 1 chronon services).

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• A site is rebuilt by make down-local && make up-local. No state lives outside git, except the CA, which is minted fresh (ADR-0007).
  • App-of-apps waves need the argoproj.io/Application health check restored in argocd-cm; the bootstrap does it.
  • Argo CD reads GitHub, so every change is a push.

docs.title: Measured numbers
docs.text: What Value Command kind cluster (3 nodes) created 91 s scripts/bootstrap/local.sh stage stamps (.logs/bootstrap-1.log) Cilium installed and cilium status --wait OK 200 s same, stage 3 → 4 Argo CD installed and rolled out 109 s same (bootstrap-2.log), stage 5 → 6 Full rebuild from git to be measured Tue 07:30 time make down-local && time make up-local

docs.title: ADR-0003: No secrets in git this round
docs.text: Status: accepted (draft) · Mon 19 Oct 2026

docs.title: Context
docs.text: GitOps wants everything in git, and secrets can't go there in plain text. Today nothing needs one: CloudNativePG generates its own database credentials in-cluster, the CA is minted in-cluster by cert-manager, and the token provider's private key stays on the operator's laptop.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Where it breaks A. No secrets in git until one is needed The day a real external credential appears (a registry token, an SSO client secret), a mechanism has to be chosen under time pressure. B. Sealed Secrets (controller key decrypts in-cluster) The controller's private key is per cluster: back it up or bring your own, or a rebuilt site can't decrypt its own repo. C. SOPS + age through an Argo CD plugin Readable diffs and per-file keys, but one more moving part to bootstrap before Argo CD can sync anything. D. External Secrets Operator Needs a secret backend (Vault, a cloud KMS) that a lab site may not have.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: A. When a secret appears, B with a bring-your-own key shared by every site, so a rebuilt cluster can decrypt immediately.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• make seal exists and says so instead of pretending.
  • .gitignore excludes .tokens/, .certs/, *.pem and *.key.

docs.title: Measured numbers
docs.text: None yet.

docs.title: ADR-0006: Cilium Gateway API in host-network mode for the local site
docs.text: Status: accepted (draft) · Mon 19 Oct 2026

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Clients reach the site through one HTTPS endpoint, with TLS and HTTP/2 (the client refuses HTTP/1.1). kind has no load balancer, and on Docker Desktop for Mac the laptop can't route to the kind network's container IPs.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Where it breaks A. Cilium Gateway, Envoy on the node's host network, on nodes labelled chronon.io/gateway=true; kind maps 8443/8080 to the laptop One node is the entry point: no failover. Ports below 1024 would need NET_BIND_SERVICE, hence 8443/8080. B. Gateway behind a LoadBalancer Service with Cilium LB-IPAM + L2 announcements The right shape for a multi-node site on a flat L2 network. Here the IP lives on a network the Mac can't reach, so it still needs a port-forward. C. BGP from Cilium to a top-of-rack router (ECMP) The production shape for a real datacenter. No router here. D. MetalLB, kube-vip, or NodePort + DNAT Duplicate what Cilium already provides, or expose high ports and a second hop. E. kubectl port-forward to the Gateway's Service Works anywhere; one more manual process that dies silently. Kept as the kill-switch fallback.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: A for the local site. gatewayAPI.enableAlpn: true so TLS listeners offer h2; its chart default is false. B for a multi-node site, C for a datacenter with a router.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Shortcut: a single entry node, named as such in the docs.
  • Backends get HTTP/1.1 from Envoy; only the edge speaks h2.

docs.title: Measured numbers
docs.text: What Value Command TLS + ALPN through the Gateway ALPN: server accepted h2, HTTP/2 200 curl --http2 -v --cacert .certs/ca.pem https://api.chronon.test:8443/healthz With the client's transport settings HTTP/2 200 httpx.Client(http2=True, http1=False).get(...)

docs.title: ADR-0007: A private CA in cert-manager for the local site
docs.text: Status: accepted (draft) · Mon 19 Oct 2026

docs.title: Context
docs.text: The client verifies TLS certificates. The local site has no public DNS, so public CAs can't issue for *.chronon.test.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Where it breaks A. cert-manager: self-signed issuer → CA certificate → CA issuer → one explicit serving Certificate; clients trust the exported CA Every rebuild mints a new CA; clients must re-export it (make ca). B. mkcert on the laptop The CA lives outside the cluster and outside git; a rebuilt site can't recreate it, and the setup is per laptop. C. A self-signed certificate per service Every client trusts every leaf; rotation means touching every client. D. Let's Encrypt (HTTP-01 through the Gateway, or DNS-01) Needs a public name. The right choice for a public site, not for .test.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: A for the local site; D (HTTP-01 through the Gateway) for a public one. Usages are explicit: the CA has cert sign, crl sign, digital signature, key encipherment; the leaf has server auth, digital signature, key encipherment. Stricter TLS stacks reject a CA without signing usages or a leaf without serverAuth (for example Python 3.13's default VERIFY_X509_STRICT). The client environment here is Python 3.12; this has not been tested against 3.13 yet.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• One trust anchor: SSL_CERT_FILE=.certs/ca.pem.
  • No cert-manager Gateway shim: the listener names its Secret, visible in git.

docs.title: Measured numbers
docs.text: What Value Command Chain verifies end to end SSL certificate verify ok, issuer CN=chronon local CA curl -v --cacert .certs/ca.pem https://api.chronon.test:8443/healthz

docs.title: What it is
docs.text: Argo CD v3.5.5 keeps the cluster equal to main. One root Application (clusters/local/bootstrap/root-app.yaml) points at clusters/local/apps/, which holds one Application per component. That's the app-of-apps pattern. Every change after bootstrap is a git commit.

docs.title: Why it's built this way
docs.text:
• Substrate below GitOps. Argo CD can't install the network it runs on, or itself, so the bootstrap script installs Cilium and Argo CD (ADR-0002).
  • Sync waves order the platform:
Wave Applications −2 cert-manager (and its CRDs) −1 CNPG operator, PKI (issuers and the serving Certificate) 0 Valkey, Argo Workflows, Gateway 1 chronon services, each with its own HTTPRoute
  • Waves only wait if Applications have health. Argo CD removed health assessment for Application resources in 1.8. Without it, wave −1 would apply ClusterIssuers before cert-manager's CRDs exist. The bootstrap restores it in argocd-cm.
  • Server-Side Apply and Server-Side Diff. SSA avoids the size limit of client-side apply's annotation on large CRDs. Server-side diff (in argocd-cmd-params-cm) lets the API server compute the predicted state, so fields it defaults don't show up as permanent drift.
  • Helm charts with values from git: each chart Application has two sources, the chart repo and this repo (ref: values), so values files are versioned with everything else.

docs.title: How it fails
docs.text:
• An app stuck Progressing holds back every later wave. Example from this build: an HTTPRoute in wave 1 waited for a Gateway in wave 2, a deadlock. Fix: the Gateway moved to wave 0.
  • OutOfSync right after a successful sync. The live object has defaulted fields that git doesn't. Server-side diff fixes it.
  • A running sync uses the revision it started with. Pushing a fix doesn't unstick it; terminate the operation first.
  • Argo CD reads GitHub, not the laptop. Unpushed commits don't exist for the cluster.

docs.title: How to debug it
docs.text:
kubectl config set-context --current --namespace=argocd
argocd login --core                       # CLI straight to the API, no server login
argocd app list
argocd app get <app>                      # per-resource sync and health
argocd app terminate-op root              # unstick a sync waiting on an old revision
kubectl -n argocd annotate application <app> argocd.argoproj.io/refresh=hard --overwrite
kubectl -n argocd logs sts/argocd-application-controller --since=5m | grep <app>
kubectl -n argocd port-forward svc/argocd-server 8081:443   # UI at https://localhost:8081
argocd admin initial-password -n argocd   # UI password for user admin

Note: since Argo CD 3.0, per-resource health is no longer stored in the Application's .status.resources. Use argocd app get or the UI.

docs.title: What it is
docs.text:
cert-manager v1.21.2 mints and renews certificates from Kubernetes resources. The local site has its own small PKI (public-key infrastructure), all in git:

ClusterIssuer selfsigned
  └─ signs Certificate chronon-ca (isCA, 1 year)  → Secret cert-manager/chronon-ca
       └─ backs ClusterIssuer chronon-ca
            └─ signs Certificate chronon-tls (90 days) → Secret gateway/chronon-tls
                 └─ referenced by the Gateway's HTTPS listener (8443)

The serving certificate covers api, state, argocd and hubble.chronon.test.

docs.title: Why it's built this way
docs.text:
• A CA, not self-signed leaves. Clients trust one file (make ca writes .certs/ca.pem); leaves rotate without touching clients (ADR-0007).
  • Usages are explicit. CA: cert sign, crl sign, digital signature, key encipherment; leaf: server auth, digital signature, key encipherment. Stricter TLS stacks (Python 3.13's default VERIFY_X509_STRICT) reject a CA without signing usages, or a leaf without serverAuth.
  • One explicit Certificate, no Gateway shim. The listener names its Secret directly, so what's served is visible in git.
  • Inside the cluster. A rebuilt site recreates its PKI from git. The cost: every rebuild mints a new CA, so re-run make ca after make up-local.

docs.title: How it fails
docs.text:
• CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED in the client or curl. Stale ca.pem from an earlier cluster: run make ca and set SSL_CERT_FILE=.certs/ca.pem.
  • Certificate stuck Ready=False. The issuer isn't ready (its Secret is missing), or cert-manager's webhook isn't up yet.
  • Gateway listener ResolvedRefs=False. The Secret chronon-tls is missing in namespace gateway.

docs.title: How to debug it
docs.text:
kubectl get clusterissuer
kubectl get certificate,certificaterequest -A
kubectl -n gateway describe certificate chronon-tls
make ca                                            # prints subject and expiry
openssl s_client -connect api.chronon.test:8443 -servername api.chronon.test \
  -CAfile .certs/ca.pem -alpn h2 </dev/null 2>/dev/null | grep -E 'Verify|ALPN'

docs.title: What it is
docs.text: Cilium 1.20.3 is the cluster's network. It gives every pod an address (CNI), load-balances Services in eBPF instead of kube-proxy's iptables chains (kubeProxyReplacement: true), runs the Envoy that implements the Gateway API, and records every flow for Hubble.

docs.title: Why it's here, and why it's installed by script
docs.text:
Nothing schedules without a CNI: pods, Argo CD's included, never get an address. So Cilium is part of the substrate that scripts/bootstrap/local.sh installs with Helm, before Argo CD exists (ADR-0002). Its values live in git anyway (platform/cilium/values.yaml plus clusters/local/values/cilium.yaml), so the install is still reproducible from the repo.

Choices that matter:

Setting Why k8sServiceHost: chronon-control-plane, port 6443 With no kube-proxy, nothing translates the kubernetes Service IP until Cilium runs, so Cilium needs the API server's real address. gatewayAPI.enableAlpn: true Defaults to false. Without it TLS listeners offer only HTTP/1.1, and the client refuses HTTP/1.1. gatewayAPI.hostNetwork on nodes labelled chronon.io/gateway=true kind has no load balancer; Envoy binds 8443/8080 on the control-plane node, and kind maps them to the laptop (ADR-0006). Shortcut. Gateway API CRDs installed before Cilium gatewayClass.create: auto creates the cilium GatewayClass only if the CRDs already exist.

docs.title: How it fails
docs.text:
• Nodes NotReady right after kind create. That's expected until Cilium is up; the bootstrap waits for it.
  • No cilium GatewayClass. The CRDs were installed after Cilium. Re-run the Helm upgrade, or restart the operator.
  • curl connects but gets HTTP/1.1, or the client fails with a protocol error. ALPN is off (cilium config view | grep alpn).
  • Connection refused on :8443. No Gateway, or no listener on that port, or the Envoy DaemonSet isn't running on the labelled node.

docs.title: How to debug it
docs.text:
cilium status                                    # agents, operator, Envoy, Hubble
cilium config view | grep -E 'kube-proxy-replacement|gateway-api'
kubectl get gatewayclass,gateway -A               # Accepted / Programmed conditions
kubectl -n gateway describe gateway chronon
kubectl -n kube-system port-forward svc/hubble-ui 12000:80   # http://localhost:12000
kubectl -n kube-system exec ds/cilium -c cilium-agent -- \
  hubble observe --verdict DROPPED --last 20      # flows dropped on that node

docs.title: What it is
docs.text: scripts/client_patch.py is a module that every test, script or notebook using the real iqcc-cloud-client imports first. It points the unmodified client at a chronon site and makes it impossible for that process to reach the upstream service.

docs.title: Why it's here
docs.text:
The client can't be pointed elsewhere by configuration alone:

  • The task API URL is a constructor argument, but without an explicit token the constructor reads ~/.config/iqcc_cloud/config.toml, whose url key overrides it.
  • The state service URL is the default of a parameter on a property (IQCC_Cloud.state). Properties take no arguments, so the default is always used, and the constructor calls it three times before returning.

So the patch works on the class, before construction:

Layer What it does IQCC_Cloud.state replaced with a property returning a StateService bound to CHRONON_STATE_URL IQCC_Cloud.data replaced with a property that raises: the datastore isn't part of chronon IQCC_Cloud.__init__ wrapped: requires api_token, refuses an upstream url and any datastore httpx.Client.send, httpx.AsyncClient.send guarded: any request whose host is the upstream domain or a subdomain raises ForbiddenHostError before it is sent

The first three make the client work against chronon. The last one is a backstop that makes a mistake fail loudly instead of sending a request. It covers code paths the first three miss.

docs.title: How it fails
docs.text:
• Not imported, or imported too late. The guard is installed by the same import, so it can't protect a process that never imported the patch. If IQCC_Cloud(...) runs first, its constructor contacts the upstream state service before anything is patched. The guard only catches code paths missed by a patch that is loaded. Defences for a forgotten import are structural: entry points that use the client (contract-test conftest.py, scripts/connect.py) import the patch themselves; an /etc/hosts sinkhole on the laptop is the OS-level backstop.
  • Wrong or missing env vars. The defaults are https://api.chronon.test:8443 and https://state.chronon.test:8443. If the site isn't up, or /etc/hosts lacks the names, httpx raises ConnectError.
  • TLS. The client verifies certificates. Against the local CA, set SSL_CERT_FILE to the CA bundle, or the handshake fails with CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED.
  • A future client version could rename state, or call another HTTP library. The guard covers httpx only, and the unit tests pin the behaviour for 0.20.0.

docs.title: How to debug it
docs.text:
uv run --extra dev pytest -q tests/unit/test_client_patch.py -v
uv run --extra dev python -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0, 'scripts'); \
  import client_patch as p; print(p.CHRONON_URL, p.CHRONON_STATE_URL)"

docs.title: What it is
docs.text:
One Python package (chronon, under src/) for every service and worker, plus Kubernetes manifests laid out by site and component, plus docs. The architecture page lists every path and whether it exists yet.

src/chronon/        one package: auth, contract, api, state, queue, db,
                    worker, arc, instrument
tests/unit/         fast tests, run by `make check`
tests/contract/     the real client against a running site (`make contract`)
scripts/            client_patch.py, and later bootstrap, rehearsal, tokens
vendor/             the client sdist: read-only reference
clusters/<site>/    what one site runs (bootstrap, Argo CD apps, values)
platform/<comp>/    shared component config reused by every site
backends/<name>/    per-backend manifests (sim-qpu, arc)
services/k8s/base/  the API and state services
docs/               this site

docs.title: Why it's built this way
docs.text:
• One package, several entry points. The API, state service and workers share models (contract.py), auth and DB code. One package means one image and one version, and a change to a shared model can't drift between services. The cost: every image carries all the code. The ARC dependencies are heavy, so they live behind an extra (chronon[arc]) and a second image target.
  • src/ layout. Tests import the installed package, not the working directory, so a missing file in the package shows up in tests rather than in production.
  • clusters/<site> over platform/*. A site is a thin overlay; shared config is written once. A second site means a new clusters/<site>/, not a copy of everything.
  • vendor/ is reference, not a dependency. The client is installed from PyPI (pinned ==0.20.0 in the dev extra); vendor/ holds the same sdist so its source can be read and cited line by line.

docs.title: How it fails
docs.text:
• Missing extra. uv run pyright without --extra dev fails with "pyright not found". The Makefile always passes --extra dev.
  • Domain gate. make check fails if the upstream service domain appears outside the allow-listed files; the output names the file and line.
  • Manifest gate. Any kustomization.yaml under clusters/, platform/, backends/ or services/k8s/base is rendered and validated. A render or schema error fails make check (pipefail is on).

docs.title: How to debug it
docs.text:
make help                         # every target and what it does
uv sync --extra dev               # rebuild the environment from uv.lock
make check                        # run the gates; the first failing one stops
uv run --extra dev pytest -q tests/unit -k client_patch   # one test file
kustomize build platform/<comp> | kubeconform -strict -summary
